title: Artificial Neural Networks for Realized Volatility Prediction in Cryptocurrency Time Series
source_type: Springer typeset chapter copy in an academic thesis bibliography; not a newly accessed publisher landing page
publication_identity_evidence: PDF page 1 / printed p.165: authors, title, Springer Nature 2019 copyright, H. Lu et al. (Eds.), ISNN 2019, LNCS 11554, pp.165–172 and DOI. PDF metadata agrees on title and DOI.
indexing_and_quartile: Not verified; publisher DOI is not evidence of WoS/Scopus coverage or Q1

dataset.provider: Kaggle Bitcoin historical data, mczielinski/bitcoin-historical-data; Ref.2, p.172
dataset.quality_rule: Missing prices and non-adjacent returns removed (Fig.3, p.167)

target.name: Realized volatility, RV
target.formal_definition: Sum of squared minute logarithmic returns within an aggregation bin:RV(t)=sum_i R_i^2
target.horizon: Future RV values predicted from past RV samples in a three-hour series; an explicit step-indexed forecast horizon is not given.
target.model_input: Past RV samples (abstract, p.165); sequence length varies by model.
target.target_transform_for_fitting: Not clearly reported. Fig.7b plots log differences but does not establish the training target transform.
target.E1_difference: Different provider and period; three-hour sums of squared minute returns versus E1 daily rolling seven-return population standard deviation; past RV versus E1 OHLCV-only inputs.

training_evaluation.reported_CV: 10-fold cross-validation for time series using 100 runs, as stated on p.170.
training_evaluation.paired_tests_or_multiplicity: Not reported in the inspected eight-page chapter.

metrics_scale: MSE and RMSE as reported. Target transformation and aggregation documentation do not establish equivalence with the E1 sigma7 scale.
reported_dispersion: Table1 labels dispersion as var = variance, not standard deviation.
critical_assessment: Primary applied Bitcoin-volatility evidence of independent MLP and CNN comparators; it does not establish that the E1 configurations were selected from this paper before training.
One additional study does not establish frequent use. Count each family once despite the two MLP variants.
The E1 one-hidden-layer MLP and causal Conv1D implementation are project adaptations, not replicas of the paper configurations.
CNN dimensionality, widths, kernels and causality are not documented; preserve those unknowns.
Split dates, scaling scope and purging rules are absent; no absence-of-leakage certification is possible.
Table1 reports HARRV lags 1,6,16 while the conclusion mentions 2,3,4; preserve the source discrepancy.
No paired comparison or confidence interval is reported. Initialization variances do not demonstrate statistically significant superiority.
Do not rank literature RMSE directly against E1 RMSE: targets, inputs, frequency, cohorts and sources differ.
review_timing: Targeted documentary recovery after the completed benchmark; not a pretraining architecture-selection record
